binary.reason: DecodeHiveBinaryFrame branches on BINARY: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. ListenBinary delivers it. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself.

control.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. The authorization-code grant with PKCE is covered here alongside the device grant: the challenge is checked to be S256 of the verifier, the verifier never to reach the browser, a redirect answering a different attempt or carrying error= to be refused, and the token exchange to refuse cleartext to a non-loopback host.

mesh.reason: ListenHive over the five hive kinds, and Propagate/Escalate/Broadcast. The kinds used to fall off the end of dispatchNoiseMessage with no case and no log line. Run against the shared mesh vectors.

refusal.reason: refusalBelongsToAsk() and failureError() in errors.go, used by AskWithOptions() in client.go, which counts asks, queries and fire-and-forget utterances inside the shared grace window -- recorded immediately before the publish and kept when the publish errors, since the transport can fail after the hub holds the frame. PolicyDeniedError carries Quota and UnansweredError is new, both still errors.Is ErrRuntime. Run against the shared refusal vectors, decoded as map[string]any so numbers arrive as float64, plus five end-to-end asks.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.
